title: Compare two populations using measures of center and variability from random samples

sections.skill: Compare two populations using measures of center and variability from random samples

questions.skill: Compare two populations using measures of center and variability from random samples
questions.prompt: Random samples of quiz scores: Class A has a median of 78 and an IQR of 10. Class B has a median of 70 and an IQR of 10. What do the samples suggest about the two classes? Use both the center and the spread.
questions.prompt_markup:
Random samples of quiz scores: Class A has a median of 78 and an IQR of 10. Class B has a median of 70 and an IQR of 10.
What do the samples suggest about the two classes? Use both the center and the spread.
questions.correct_answer: The samples suggest Class A tends to score higher, by about 8 points (median). The spreads are the same (IQR 10), so the scores overlap and some Class B students may score higher than some Class A students.
questions.grading_note: Full credit uses both the centers and the spreads and states a tendency, not a certainty about every student.

questions.skill: Compare two populations using measures of center and variability from random samples
questions.prompt: A random sample of 7th graders has a mean of 6.5 hours of screen time and a MAD of 1.2. A random sample of 8th graders has a mean of 7.7 hours and a MAD of 1.2. Write the difference in means as a multiple of the MAD. What does this suggest about the two populations?
questions.prompt_markup:
A random sample of 7th graders has a mean of 6.5 hours of screen time and a MAD of 1.2. A random sample of 8th graders has a mean of 7.7 hours and a MAD of 1.2.
Write the difference in means as a multiple of the MAD. What does this suggest about the two populations?
questions.correct_answer: 1 MAD. The samples suggest 8th graders tend to have more screen time, but the distributions overlap a lot, so the difference is modest.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: 1 MAD, and an inference that uses the overlap.
